evidenceAudit.scope: Long-term outpatient care of adults with compensated and decompensated cirrhosis in India: diagnosis and staging, treatment of the cause, non-selective beta-blockers to prevent variceal bleeding and decompensation, variceal and hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) surveillance, prevention of spontaneous bacterial peritonitis, nutrition, vaccination and referral, using NICE NG50, AASLD portal hypertension guidance (2023) and the BSG/BASL ascites guideline, because no Indian national cirrhosis guideline with doses could be opened.
findings: Transient elastography, hepatology referral, MELD every 6 months (12 or more = high risk), ultrasound with or without alpha-fetoprotein every 6 months for HCC, endoscopy at diagnosis unless starting a beta-blocker and every 3 years if no varices, carvedilol first choice (start 6.25 mg/day) and propranolol second choice (start 40 mg twice daily), band ligation if beta-blockers not tolerated, carvedilol avoided in refractory ascites, and selective SBP prophylaxis (ascitic protein 15 g/L or less, Child-Pugh above 9 or MELD above 16) checked against NICE NG50.

Carvedilol 12.5 mg/day target, dose reduction if systolic BP below 90 mmHg, endoscopy intervals off beta-blocker (2 years active disease, 3 years controlled, yearly decompensated) and band ligation every 2–4 weeks to obliteration checked against the AASLD 2023 guidance slide summary.
Norfloxacin 400 mg daily or ciprofloxacin 500 mg daily for SBP prophylaxis from BSG/BASL 2020 recommendation 2.8.
unverifiedSections: INASL and Baveno VII full texts were not opened; Baveno VII use of liver stiffness 25 kPa or more for clinically significant portal hypertension is from a secondary summary and is not used to drive treatment here.
The AASLD guidance was read as a slide summary, not the full text.
Nutrition targets (protein and late-evening snack) are general practice and not quoted from an opened source.
Hepatitis A and B vaccination is standard practice; doses are not given.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Cirrhosis is the end stage of chronic liver injury. In India the main causes are alcohol, hepatitis B and C, and metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD). Patients are compensated for years and then decompensate with ascites, variceal bleeding, encephalopathy or jaundice. Good long-term care treats the cause (abstinence, antivirals, weight loss), lowers portal pressure with carvedilol to prevent bleeding and decompensation, screens for varices and HCC every 6 months, prevents infection in high-risk ascites, protects nutrition and kidneys (avoid NSAIDs), and refers early for transplant assessment when MELD rises.
keyMechanisms: Chronic injury causes fibrosis and nodules that raise intrahepatic resistance (portal hypertension).
Portal hypertension causes varices, ascites and splenomegaly.
Non-selective beta-blockers lower portal inflow; carvedilol also lowers intrahepatic resistance.
Bacterial translocation causes SBP; loss of synthetic function causes coagulopathy and low albumin.

redFlags: Gastrointestinal bleeding: emergency (see Upper GI bleeding topic)
Fever or abdominal pain with ascites: tap for SBP
Rising creatinine or sodium below 125 mmol/L

clinicalManagement.title: Treat the cause
actions: Stop alcohol; antivirals for hepatitis B or C; weight loss for MASLD.

clinicalManagement.title: Prevent bleeding and decompensation
actions: Reduce dose if systolic BP below 90 mmHg (AASLD).
Band ligation if beta-blockers not tolerated (NICE 1.3.5).

clinicalManagement.title: Surveillance
actions: Ultrasound with or without AFP; MELD (NICE 1.2.2, 1.2.4).
Endoscopy as per intervals if not on a beta-blocker (NICE; AASLD).

clinicalManagement.title: Protect the patient
actions: Avoid NSAIDs and sedatives; vaccinate against hepatitis A and B.
SBP prophylaxis only for high-risk ascites (NICE 1.3.7; BSG/BASL).
Adequate protein and energy; late-evening snack.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
actions: Specialist hepatology centre for complications or high risk (NICE 1.2.1); transplant assessment.

patientEducation: Avoid painkillers like ibuprofen and diclofenac.
Seek care for bleeding, confusion, fever or abdominal swelling.
lifestyleAndDiet: Small frequent meals with adequate protein; late-evening snack; salt restriction if ascites.
nonClinicalManagement.followUpPlan: Review every 6 months with ultrasound, MELD and medicine check; sooner after any decompensation (NICE).
